Alright, let me think this through as myself — sitting down at the table with my notebook before the season really kicks off.

---

## My reasoning

I'm 42, five years into farming after coming back to the village. With only 6 mu, I'm not going to get rich from grain — honestly, if my wife's off-farm wages disappeared tomorrow, we'd be in trouble. But I treat this plot seriously. I read the extension bulletins, I went to a soil-testing session at the county agritech station two years ago, and I keep a simple field log on my phone: sowing date, fertilizer applied, irrigation dates, final yield, weather notes. That's my main advantage over the older uncles around me — I have actual numbers from my own field to reason from.

The system is wheat-maize double crop, same 6 mu rotating through both. That's basically locked in — it's what the soil, the water infrastructure, and the market are set up for here. Switching to cotton or vegetables on 6 mu doesn't pencil out given my off-farm schedule; grain is low-touch and fits around my other work.

**On wheat (my main cash concern):** Last year I got about 490 kg/mu with 17.5 kg N/mu split base-and-topdress. The year before, I over-applied at jointing and got lodging in a wet patch — cost me maybe 30 kg/mu on that strip. So this year I'm sticking with the split but keeping topdress a bit more conservative. Target 500 kg/mu, which is reasonable for my soil (medium loam, OM around 1.4% based on the test I paid for). Base fertilizer is a 15-15-15 compound at 40 kg/mu plus 10 kg urea; topdress at jointing with 18-20 kg urea depending on how the crop looks. I'll skip topdress-2 at booting — my data doesn't show it pays back on my field.

**On irrigation:** Well electricity is around 25-30 yuan per mu per event. Wheat gets winter water (if December stays dry), green-up in early March, jointing in early April, and grain-fill in mid-May. Four events is my default; I'll drop the winter one if we get good snow. Maize usually only needs the big-trumpet irrigation unless July-August rains fail.

**On maize:** No-till direct seeding right after wheat harvest — I rent the seeder from a neighbor for 15 yuan/mu, saves me three days of tillage which matters because the wheat-to-maize window is maybe 5 days. Hybrid seed (Zhengdan 958 type), base compound at planting, topdress urea at V8. Target 550 kg/mu. Corn borer pressure was moderate last year so I'll do one insecticide spray at tasseling.

**On pesticides:** Herbicide is non-negotiable on both crops — I can't hand-weed 6 mu and hold down the other work. Fungicide on wheat only if I see rust or powdery mildew at flag leaf.

**On labor:** My wife and I handle everything except combine harvest and seeding, which I hire. Our two kids are in school, so labor is basically just us two.

**On budget:** I'm budgeting around 2,800 yuan total inputs for the year across both crops. That's about 470 yuan/mu per crop, which I can cover from off-farm savings without needing credit. If grain prices drop sharply I might trim the maize topdress, but otherwise the plan holds.
